Name: Richard Hooker
Summary: English theologian (1554-1600) whose defence of the Church of England gave Anglicanism its classic account of Scripture, tradition, and reason.
Contribution: His Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity argued that Scripture, reason, and the church's traditions together guide the church's life, answering Puritan calls to remake worship on a single pattern. His reasoning still underpins Anglican identity.
KeyWorks: Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity
Testimony: A parish priest as well as a scholar, he spent his final years writing while serving a country parish.
